# ADR-PD-0005 — Ingress path prefixing is generated by the wrapper kustomization, not hand-typed by the actor author

## Context

`recipe` and `environment.name` never meet anywhere in this package. `recipe` is consumed exactly
once, by `_overlay_dir()`, to pick a folder on disk at render time; `environment.name` is consumed
exactly once, as the `-n <namespace>` argument to `ensure_namespace()`/`kubectl apply`. Neither
value is ever written into a rendered object.

Yet every actor-authored `Ingress` (`examples/customer/deploy/k8s/overlays/develop/ingress.yaml`,
`examples/waiter/...`, and the equivalent in the consumer product
`papeete-actor-synchronous-messaging-http`'s "table-service" example) hand-types a URL path prefix
that happens to spell the recipe/environment names — a coincidence of authoring discipline, not a
structural reference to anything. `ADR-PD-0004` already hit the resulting collision for real
(ingress-nginx's admission webhook enforces host+path uniqueness cluster-wide, and an unprefixed
path collided with an already-deployed instance) and fixed it the only way available at the time:
by hand-editing the literal path string to include a product+recipe prefix, the same class of fix
that ADR's own namePrefix had just made unnecessary for object *names*. That was documented there
as authored-not-injected, "exactly the kind of literal value `namePrefix` structurally cannot
reach" — true of `namePrefix` specifically, but not the final word: nothing else in this package
reaches it either, so two environments deployed from the *same* recipe (a PR-preview namespace and
a long-lived dev namespace, both using the `develop` overlay) still collide on identical Ingress
paths today. This ADR closes that gap the same way `namePrefix` closed it for names: generate the
prefix at apply time instead of trusting an author to keep it in sync by hand.

## Decision

Extend `_wrapper_kustomization()` (already the one seam that injects `namePrefix`/`commonLabels`/
`images` into every rendered manifest) to also inject, unconditionally, on every wrapper it builds
— actor-level (`apply()`) and product-level (`apply_product()`) alike, no per-actor opt-in:

1. A `configMapGenerator` producing one throwaway ConfigMap whose data holds a single literal:
   `PATH_PREFIX=/<normalize_name(product_name)>/<namespace>` (`namespace` is `environment.name`,
   already namespace-safe and therefore URL-segment-safe; `product_name` is normalized the same
   way `namePrefix` already normalizes it, for the same reason — a clean URL segment).
2. A `replacements` block whose `source` is that ConfigMap's `data.PATH_PREFIX`, targeting every
   `Ingress` object (`select: {kind: Ingress}`, unfiltered by name) at
   `fieldPaths: [spec.rules.*.http.paths.*.path]`, with `options: {delimiter: '/', index: 0}`.

Both `product_name` and `namespace` are already parameters on `apply()`/`apply_product()` today —
`namespace` currently stops at `ensure_namespace()`/the `-n` flag and never reaches
`_wrapper_kustomization()`. The only signature change is threading it one level further in:

```
_wrapper_kustomization(overlay_dir, image_name, resolved_version, product_name, namespace)
```

No new CLI flag, no new `product.yaml` field, no change to `deploy()`'s call sites beyond passing
the value it already has.

Consumer-authored `ingress.yaml` files own only their bare, actor-local path segment going
forward — e.g. `path: /customer/api(/|$)(.*)`, no product, no environment, nothing left for a
human to keep in sync.

## Rationale

**Why `replacements` reaches this at all.** Investigated live (`kubectl kustomize`, kustomize
v5.7.1, shipped with kubectl 1.34) rather than assumed from docs. `replacements` is not a generic
string-concatenation primitive — every mode of it *replaces* a target field/segment wholesale with
a source field's value; it never appends one field's value onto another's. The prefix effect used
here is a side effect of a more specific, verified mechanism: with `options.delimiter` set,
kustomize splits the target field into parts and replaces exactly one part (selected by
`options.index`) with the source value. On an absolute path — which by definition starts with
`/`, so splitting on `/` always yields an empty first element — `index: 0` (also the observed
default when omitted) replaces that empty leading element with the full source string. Verified
concretely:

```
target: aaa/bbb/ccc         source: ZZZ    index: 0  → ZZZ/bbb/ccc   (replaces, not prefixes)
target: /customer/api(/|$)(.*)   source: /table-service/develop   index: 0 (default)
  → /table-service/develop/customer/api(/|$)(.*)                   (clean prefix — because
                                                                      segment 0 was already "")
```

Also verified: `fieldPaths` wildcards (`spec.rules.*.http.paths.*.path`) correctly reach every
rule and every path across multiple `Ingress` objects in one `replacements` entry; and a wrapper
with no `Ingress` object in its overlay at all renders cleanly with no error — the `select` simply
matches nothing. Both properties are what make "inject unconditionally, no per-actor opt-in" safe.

**Why this depends on a leading `/`.** The replace-index-0 trick is only a clean prefix *because*
segment 0 of an absolute path is empty. A path authored without a leading `/` would have its real
first segment silently replaced (data loss, not a hard failure) instead of prefixed. This is not a
new constraint this ADR imposes — the Kubernetes API already requires every `HTTPIngressPath.path`
to start with `/` — but it is a correctness dependency worth stating explicitly, since nothing here
would surface a violation loudly.

**Why a synthesized ConfigMap instead of an inline literal.** `replacements`' `source` must
reference a field on an actual object in the resource set — there is no inline-literal source
form. A `configMapGenerator`-produced ConfigMap is the standard, minimal vehicle for handing
`replacements` a literal to point at. It picks up the same `commonLabels` every other wrapper
object gets, so `delete()`'s existing label-swept teardown (`all,configmap,ingress` by
`papeete-deploy/product=<name>`) reclaims it with no separate handling — it was already sweeping
`configmap`.

**Why not the Python text-substitution fallback.** That was the fallback under consideration if
kustomize turned out to only support whole-field replacement with no way to preserve the rest of
the string. It doesn't turn out that way — `replacements` reaches this natively via the
delimiter/index mechanism above — so the fallback isn't needed. Staying on kustomize-only
machinery keeps `k8s.py`'s existing policy intact: it generates fresh wrapper YAML, and otherwise
never reads or parses an actor's own manifest content.

**Why unconditional, no per-actor opt-in.** Same precedent `ADR-PD-0004` set for `namePrefix`:
apply it to every wrapper, no exceptions, rather than adding a flag an author could forget to set
— the entire motivation here is removing a "must remember to do this by hand" failure mode, so the
fix shouldn't reintroduce a smaller version of the same failure mode.

## Consequences

- **Breaking change requiring coordinated updates, with a silent (not loud) failure mode.**
  `examples/customer/deploy/k8s/overlays/develop/ingress.yaml`,
  `examples/waiter/deploy/k8s/overlays/develop/ingress.yaml`, and the equivalent file(s) in the
  `papeete-actor-synchronous-messaging-http` "table-service" consumer example all need their
  hand-typed `/table-service/develop/...` prefixes dropped back down to their bare actor-local
  segment. This is the same shape of breaking change `ADR-PD-0004`'s `namePrefix` rename already
  was, but worse in one respect: `namePrefix` breaks loudly (old bare names simply don't exist,
  clients fail to resolve them), whereas an un-migrated `ingress.yaml` deployed against a
  papeete-deploy version carrying this change would render successfully with a *doubled*, merely
  wrong path (e.g. `/table-service/develop/table-service/develop/customer/api...`) — `kubectl
  apply` would not fail. Needs an explicit migration note in release notes, not just reliance on
  things breaking visibly.
- **One extra rendered object per apply.** A small throwaway ConfigMap appears in every actor's
  and the product-level apply, even for overlays with no `Ingress` at all — harmless, and already
  reclaimed by `delete()`'s existing sweep, but slightly more `kubectl get configmap` noise per
  namespace.
- **New dependency on specific `replacements` behavior.** The delimiter/index semantics were
  verified live against kustomize v5.7.1 (bundled with kubectl 1.34) — worth an offline unit test
  asserting the rendered `Ingress` path (same "offline-testable, pure string/YAML construction"
  style `_wrapper_kustomization()` already gets tested with), so a future kustomize upgrade that
  changed this behavior would be caught by the suite rather than discovered live against a
  cluster.
- No change to `product.yaml`'s schema, no new CLI flag, no change to `k8s.delete()`,
  `ensure_namespace()`, or actor-folder resolution.
- `_wrapper_kustomization()`'s signature grows one parameter (`namespace`); `apply()`/
  `apply_product()` already receive it today and just need to forward it one call further in.
